sentences.text: No, the documents do not show a conflict: the UCB rule says that at the time of reset of interest rates, a UCB may, at its option, provide a choice to the borrowers to switch over to a fixed rate as per its Board approved policy, and the policy likewise says the bank may, at its option, offer the borrower a choice to switch to a fixed rate as per its Board approved policy.

The UCB rule applies to this kind of switching framework, and it also requires that applicable charges for switching of loans from floating to fixed rate and any other service charges / administrative costs incidental to the exercise of the above options shall be transparently disclosed in the sanction letter and at the time of revision of such charges / costs.

The documents do not state any conflict between the policy wording and the current UCB rule; the rule finding is still unknown only on applicability by rate_type, and the evidence does not state the loan’s rate_type.

missing.searched: whether the retail loan is floating rate or another rate_type
